title: Structure a delivery-reliability problem
scenario: QuickCart's on-time delivery rate fell from 91% to 79%, mostly during evening peaks, while total weekly orders stayed flat.

responseCycle.prompt: Build a testable issue tree for the reliability decline and explain where you would start.
guidance: Separate demand timing, available capacity, and process execution.

criteria.label: Separates demand, capacity, and process drivers
Makes the evening concentration testable
Chooses a starting branch using the facts given

comparison.title: One operational structure
comparison.text: Separate when orders arrive, whether courier capacity matches the peak, and whether dispatch or merchant handoff adds delay; start with peak capacity because volume is flat overall but service fails in a specific window.

title: Structure a market-entry decision
scenario: Verdant Foods is considering launching its plant-based snack line in a neighboring country. The CEO needs a go/no-go recommendation before committing a national launch budget.

responseCycle.prompt: Lay out the decision branches and state which uncertainty you would resolve first.

criteria.label: Covers attractiveness, economics, and ability to win
Keeps external demand separate from internal execution
Prioritizes the uncertainty that could stop the launch

comparison.title: One decision-led structure
comparison.text: Test whether the market is attractive, whether target consumers will buy this offer, whether unit economics work, and whether Verdant can reach customers; validate demand first because weak adoption would make the remaining launch plan irrelevant.

title: Find the broken onboarding step
scenario: Meridian Bank's completed mobile-account openings fell 22% immediately after an onboarding redesign, while application starts were unchanged.

responseCycle.prompt: Choose the next analysis and explain how it would isolate the failure point.
guidance: Use the timing and stable application starts to narrow the search.

criteria.label: Selects an analysis that locates the broken funnel step
Uses the redesign timing to justify priority

comparison.title: One high-information move
comparison.text: Compare completion by onboarding step before and after the redesign; that directly locates where unchanged starts stop converting and tests whether the redesign caused the decline.

options.label: Compare conversion at each onboarding step before and after launch

title: Decide what to learn before rollout
scenario: UrbanEats piloted a smaller menu in 12 restaurants. Service time improved, average ticket was flat, and management is considering a national rollout.

responseCycle.prompt: Name the highest-value remaining test before rollout and the decision risk it addresses.

criteria.label: Targets a risk that matters before an expensive rollout
Tests whether the pilot effect differs across customers or stores

comparison.title: One prudent next test
comparison.text: Compare repeat visits and item substitution by customer and store segment; faster service is encouraging, but a national rollout should wait until we know whether reduced choice harms retention anywhere.

options.label: Compare repeat visits and substitution by customer and store segment
Roll out nationally because service time improved
Test a new logo in the pilot restaurants

title: Size a free-shipping pilot
scenario: HarborCart expects free shipping to add 24,000 orders per quarter. Each order brings $18 of gross profit, costs $6 to fulfill, and receives a $4 shipping subsidy. Calculate annual incremental contribution.

responseCycle.prompt: Show the per-order contribution, annualization, sense check, and decision implication before entering the result.
guidance: Calculate contribution per order before scaling volume.

criteria.label: Nets variable costs before multiplying volume
Checks that contribution remains positive per order
Explains whether the pilot creates material value

comparison.title: One complete unit-economics read
comparison.text: ($18 − $6 − $4) × 24,000 × 4 = $768,000 annually; the pilot adds positive contribution, so the decision should now test whether the projected order lift is credible.

title: Evaluate a subscription price increase
scenario: Northwind Software has 50,000 subscribers paying $20 per month. It is considering a $4 monthly increase and expects 12% of subscribers to cancel. Calculate the annual revenue change versus today.

responseCycle.prompt: Set up the retained base, reconcile new revenue to the current baseline, and state what the result does and does not prove.

criteria.label: Applies the price to the retained subscriber base
Compares new annual revenue with today's baseline
Separates revenue impact from the broader pricing decision

comparison.title: One reconciled pricing calculation
comparison.text: 50,000 × 88% × $24 × 12 − 50,000 × $20 × 12 = $672,000 of added annual revenue; the increase clears the revenue test under this churn assumption, but customer and cost effects still need validation.

title: Read a channel-mix exhibit
scenario: Beacon Retail channel results: stores grew revenue 2% at a 14% contribution margin; online grew revenue 30% at a −4% contribution margin; total revenue grew 11% while total contribution fell.

responseCycle.prompt: Interpret the exhibit using What / So what / Now what, focusing on the relationship between growth and contribution.
guidance: Compare channel growth with channel economics.

criteria.label: Identifies the shift toward fast-growing online sales
Explains why the mix shift reduces contribution
Names the online economics to investigate next

comparison.title: One mix-shift interpretation
comparison.text: Growth is concentrated online, where each sale currently loses contribution, so revenue growth is diluting profit; break online economics into fulfillment, discounting, and returns next.

options.label: Fast online growth is shifting sales toward a loss-making channel
Store revenue collapsed and caused the contribution decline
Both channels grew at the same rate and margin

title: Resolve a hidden-denominator signal
scenario: CedarCare patient complaints rose from 400 to 480 while completed visits increased from 10,000 to 15,000. Complaint categories and severity were otherwise stable.

responseCycle.prompt: Explain the numerator, denominator, resulting rate, implication, and best follow-up.

criteria.label: Evaluates complaints relative to completed visits
Recognizes that the complaint rate fell
Still tests whether a subgroup or severe issue worsened

comparison.title: One denominator-aware read
comparison.text: Complaints rose in count but fell from 4.0% to 3.2% of visits, so broad service quality did not deteriorate on this measure; check clinic-level rates and severe complaints before closing the issue.

options.label: Complaint count rose, but complaints per visit fell from 4.0% to 3.2%
The higher complaint count proves care quality worsened
Complaints rose because completed visits declined

title: Synthesize a supplier bottleneck
scenario: AeroParts' late orders increased from 6% to 18%. One supplier provides 70% of delayed components and its defect rate tripled. Internal assembly time and demand were stable. Expedite spending doubled.

responseCycle.prompt: Lead with the current cause, support it with decisive evidence, and recommend a risk-controlled next step.
guidance: Use evidence that distinguishes the supplier explanation from internal capacity.

criteria.label: States the supplier bottleneck as the current answer
Uses evidence that rules against demand or assembly
Proposes an action that protects supply continuity

comparison.title: One causal synthesis
comparison.text: The delivery decline is supplier-driven: the supplier behind most delayed parts tripled defects while demand and assembly stayed stable; qualify a backup source while requiring a corrective plan from the incumbent.

evidenceOptions.label: One supplier accounts for 70% of delayed components

nextStepOptions.label: Qualify a backup while enforcing a supplier corrective plan
Add an internal assembly shift immediately

title: Calibrate a pilot recommendation
scenario: BrightLearn tested guided onboarding with 2,000 new users. Thirty-day retention rose from 41% to 48%, support contacts fell 12%, and onboarding cost increased $3 per user. The pilot covered only one acquisition channel.

responseCycle.prompt: Give an answer-first recommendation that weighs the result, limitation, and next commitment.

criteria.label: Makes a recommendation proportional to the pilot evidence
Uses the single-channel limitation in the conclusion
Proposes a measurable expansion rather than a full rollout

comparison.title: One calibrated synthesis
comparison.text: Expand guided onboarding to a second, different channel rather than launch everywhere: retention improved and support demand fell, but the single-channel pilot does not yet prove transfer, and the added cost should be tracked against retained-user value.

evidenceOptions.label: The pilot covered one acquisition channel

nextStepOptions.label: Test a second channel and compare retained-user value with added cost
Launch to every acquisition channel immediately
